reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement. Lomitapide inhibits microsomal triglyceride transfer protein (MTTP), and the comprehensive lipid profile changes confirm this mechanism is working - VLDL-C decreased 44.8%, triglycerides decreased 44.4%, and Apo B decreased 41.4%, all consistent with MTTP inhibition blocking VLDL assembly and secretion. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear pathway modulation demonstrated. The biomarker pattern shows the expected downstream effects of MTTP inhibition - reduced VLDL assembly leads to decreased triglycerides, VLDL-C, and subsequently LDL-C. The 37.5% LDL-C reduction at week 56 confirms sustained pathway engagement. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint clearly met with 42.2% reduction in LDL-C, which is clinically meaningful for homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia patients who typically have severely elevated cholesterol despite standard therapy. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis reported, but the Japanese population with homozygous FH responded as expected. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm design limits interpretation, but the magnitude of effect (-42.2% LDL-C reduction) is well above what would be expected from placebo or natural variation in this severe genetic condition.

failure_modes.evidence: Very small sample size (N=9) limits generalizability, though effect size was large enough to demonstrate efficacy in this rare genetic condition
